name: Theocracy
description: A deity or sacred law is the supreme authority, and religious leaders guide and run the government day to day.

name: Absolute monarchy
description: The monarch holds supreme authority, which no written law, constitution or custom limits.

name: Autocracy
description: Rule by one person with absolute power, whose decisions face no outside legal limit and no regular popular control.

name: Anarchism
description: No government is compulsory: each person chooses which communities, rules or protection services to belong to, and everything is organized by voluntary agreement.

name: Partocracy
description: A single party dominates the state and decides who holds office, in place of citizens or individual representatives.

name: Representative democracy
description: Citizens elect representatives who govern for a limited time, under a constitution that protects rights.

name: Direct democracy
description: Citizens vote directly on initiatives, laws and constitutional changes, through mandatory or popular referendums, as in the Swiss model.

name: Councils
description: Power rests with councils of workers and peasants, directly elected from the bottom up, with recallable mandates.

name: Communalism
description: Citizens govern themselves in face-to-face neighborhood and municipal assemblies, which join in a regional confederation.

name: Digital democracy
description: Open networks, cryptographic voting and digital platforms allow continuous participation, direct polling and open policy-making.

name: Constitutional monarchy
description: The monarch is head of state, but their powers are limited by a constitution, and often they are only a symbol of stability.

name: Minarchism
description: The "night-watchman" state: it only protects against aggression, theft and broken contracts, and nothing more.

name: Meritocracy
description: Leadership posts go to those who stand out in exams, results and careers, not by vote or inheritance.

name: Technocracy
description: Decision-makers are chosen for their expertise in the area, especially scientific and technical knowledge.

name: Stratocracy
description: Government is headed by military commanders, and the state and the armed forces are, in practice, one and the same.

name: Aristocracy
description: Power rests with a distinguished class, who rule on the basis of inherited status, education and land held for generations.

name: Anarcho-monarchism
description: A monarch who exists only to stop a state from forming, as a symbolic protector of a society of individual liberty and voluntary cooperation.

name: Neocameralism
description: The state works like a publicly traded company, run by a professional executive and owned by shareholders, in pursuit of efficiency and order.

name: Communism
description: A society without classes or a state, with the means of production held in common and decisions taken collectively.

name: Balanced
description: No settled position on who should have the final say over the country's course.
